Paddock.body:
## New in 1.8.1

- **Custom fields in the Library.** A new **Library › Custom fields** tab lets you manage your own car fields.
  - **Add field** opens the same small window as Add option. Choose a name, a type (text, choice, number, date, yes/no or notes) and the car section where the field should show.
  - You can rename a field, move it to another section, or move it up or down within its section.
  - Before you delete a field, Paddock shows how many cars have a value in it. Deleting removes those values, but each car's history keeps a note of the old value.
- **Fields in their car section.** A custom field appears under **Your fields** in the section you chose: Technical & parts, Real Car History, Maintenance or Performance. Fields in Identity & ownership stay in Notes, as before.
  - In the edit window, Technical & parts fields are on the Technical tab. All other custom fields are on the Custom tab, grouped by section.
- **More ways to sort the Cars page:**
  - by every custom field;
  - by year of the real car, release year, purchase date, purchase price, current value and storage location.

  Numbers sort as numbers (9,50 comes before 45), yes/no sorts yes first, and cars without a value always come last.

Custom fields stay private. They are left out of car sharing, Dealership packages and car files, and they are included in complete backups. The database format is unchanged.

## Downloads

- **Windows installer:** `SlotForgePaddock-1.8.1-Setup.exe` updates the installed app and keeps your existing collection and settings.
- **Windows portable:** `SlotForgePaddock-1.8.1-Portable.exe` runs without installation.
- **Source:** `SlotForgePaddock-1.8.1-source.zip` contains the tagged source: the app, build files and tests.
- **Linux:** native x64 and ARM64 packages, each as AppImage and .deb.
- **macOS:** `SlotForgePaddock-1.8.1-mac-universal.dmg` (or the .zip), for Intel and Apple Silicon. The app is not signed with an Apple developer certificate, so macOS asks for approval the first time you open it; see the [macOS notes](https://github.com/theDutchmanJames/SlotForgePaddock/blob/main/docs/BUILDING.md).
- **Parts lists (optional):** the parts lists are attached to this release, separately from the app. See [what they contain and how to import them](https://github.com/theDutchmanJames/SlotForgePaddock/blob/main/parts-lists/README.md).

## Validation

- **Automated tests on Windows:** 1,892 tests; 1,883 passed, none failed, and nine optional tests were skipped.
- **Syntax checks:** passed for 320 JavaScript files.
- **Interface smoke test:** passed all 294 checks, including a new click-through of the custom field screens.
- **Windows package:** every application file in the package was compared with the tagged source and matches.

Timing.body:
- **Solo:** a new kind of session for driving and testing on your own. One driver and one car, on any lane: Switch lane (the Track Call button, Tab, or the button on the race page) tells Timing which lane the car is on, or it follows the car by itself. Widgets set to the new lane "Followed" show the lane the car is on, with the best lap of that lane. The results show your laps by lane and car.
- **Small things that help on a race night:**
  - The computer and its screen stay awake while a race is on.
  - **Ctrl + Shift + lane number** takes back a lap counted by hand.
  - **Undo DNF** when you check the results.
  - "Saving the results…" while a race is saved.
  - Phones reconnect at once when you tap "Reconnecting", or when they wake up, and the Race Director page names the race and the heat.
  - Start a race: **Draw lanes** (by lot, with Undo) and **Clear all**; a driver or car already on another lane is greyed out.
  - The race check says when the setup uses a deleted layout, audio set or system, or a Solo layout without Followed widgets.
  - Record Book: "Data as of" and **Refresh**.
  - Choice questions work with the arrow keys and Enter.
- **Race night safety nets:**
  - Stop in a heat race asks: **End this heat** (then the break and the next heat) or **End the event**.
  - **Retire car** on every lane card (⋯), also on the phone: the car is listed as DNF and the race no longer waits for it. Undo puts it back.
  - A **recovery pill** in the race bar says when the race was last saved for recovery, and turns red when that fails.
  - **Reconnect** in the race bar when the Trackmate or Arduino box drops out.
  - **Save results to a file** when the results cannot be saved: Import reads it back.
  - Phones and the second screen: a **Live / Reconnecting** pill, the clock stops on old data, and Race Director buttons show **Sending… / Done**, or why nothing was done.
- **Fixes from an app-wide check:**
  - Race-night risks: resuming with DS or plugin timing, remapped pit sensors, the SQLite worker restarting after a crash, a race without a limit, the championship check on Home, imports that doubled races.
  - The race: an aborted start, the Review laps panel, Space after red, timing hardware locked during a race, track power after a disconnect, a silent Trackmate.
  - Live screens and phones: reconnecting after an error, staying in step, commands for the right heat, a double-tapped Pause, logins that last, private settings kept off phones.
  - Speed: the race screen paints less while hidden or in full screen, Home, Results and the Record Book read less.
- **Changed:** with a Trackmate or Arduino box the track power now goes off at the finish and stays off through the break between heats; it comes back on at the next start.

Circuit.body:
Power taps: plan where the power base and extra feed wires join the track, and check that every lane gets enough power.

## What's new

- **Power taps:** right-click a piece and choose Power base here or Power tap here. B, T1, T2 … appear on the track.
- **Checked as you build:** Circuit flags any stretch between two feeds that is too long. On plastic track that's 10 m or 15 joints; on routed wood it depends on braid or copper tape.
- **Suggested taps:** one button adds taps where they are needed, on a straight where possible.
- **Test sheet:** type the voltage at the power base and at each test point; a lane more than 1 V down is marked.
- **In the PDF report:** a page with the feeds, the test points on the track picture and the test table.
- **Also new since v0.4.1:** the new look, better updates, faster saves and the fixes from v0.5.0.

## Details

- The power taps are in the new **Power taps** section of the Track Builder inspector (the lightning bolt). The limits can be changed for each track.
- The limits are rules of thumb from slot car guides: a feed every 5–10 m and every 12–15 joints on plastic track; braid carries one feed about 30 m, copper tape needs about five times as many. The voltage test is the real check: at any point a lane should stay within 1 V of the power base while a car is running (BSCRA track standard).
- FreeForm circuits are not supported yet, and the track must be one closed loop to be checked.
- Power marks are saved with the track. SlotForge Timing opens these tracks as before and ignores the power marks; the design revision does not change when you add taps.
- Fixed: a "ResizeObserver loop" warning when the Track sheet was shown.

## Verification

61 unit test files pass on Windows, including a new one for the power checks. 49 interface tests clicking through the real app pass on Windows. A new interface test marks a power base, adds the suggested tap, enters readings, restarts the app and saves the PDF.

## Install or update

| System | Installer | Portable app |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | `SlotForgeCircuit-0.6.0-Setup-x64.exe` | `SlotForgeCircuit-0.6.0-Portable-x64.exe` |
| macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) | `SlotForgeCircuit-0.6.0-mac-universal.dmg` | `SlotForgeCircuit-0.6.0-mac-universal.zip` |
| Linux (x64) | `SlotForgeCircuit-0.6.0-linux-amd64.deb` | `SlotForgeCircuit-0.6.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage` |
| Linux (ARM) | `SlotForgeCircuit-0.6.0-linux-arm64.deb` | `SlotForgeCircuit-0.6.0-linux-arm64.AppImage` |

Circuit is not code-signed: on Windows choose **More info → Run anyway**, or right-click the downloaded file → **Properties** → **Unblock**; on macOS right-click the app and choose **Open** the first time; on Linux mark the AppImage as executable (`chmod +x`). The SHA256SUMS files list each download's checksum.

Install over 0.5.0 or 0.4.1 as before: your saved tracks and packs stay where they are. Storage formats and the SlotForge Timing integration are unchanged.

Telemetry.body:
**SlotForge Telemetry 0.15.0 rebuilds the app around your laps and your changes: every run on one Laps wall, a Setups page that says what a change does, a Library binder, a new Track day, and the shared SlotForge look.**

### Laps: every run on one wall

Six lap pages are now one. Pick a car, then a track and lane, and every run lands on one wall, whether it came from Paddock, Track day or was typed in. Each lap is a coloured square, from green at the record to red. The page also shows the record, the pace now, how much you gained, what changed between runs (such as *pinion 9 → 10*) and which changes moved the pace. Every run can have a note and a kind (Practice, Race, …), kept apart from imported races.

### Setups: what does this change do?

Analyze is now **Setups**. Compare up to three setups, including the workbench as it is now, to see a change before you save it. You get a plain verdict ("quicker on the straight, pulls less out of a corner"), the inputs you changed, and only the results that moved, marked green or red. There is also a new result: pull per kg.

### Library, Track day, Driver Feedback and the workbench

- **Library:** every setup in one list, grouped by car, with the best lap driven on that gearing. Star favourites, tick several to compare, export or delete them, and find cars and tracks on the same page.
- **Track day:** each run of the day is a column. Change pinion, gear, weight and tyre with + and − (Telemetry records the change for you), type one lap per box, and use *Keep this change* to put the quickest run's setup back on the workbench.
- **Driver Feedback:** one page that builds up as you answer: picture cards for what the car does, short questions, a checklist, then three suggestions. One click sends a suggestion to Track day.
- **Workbench:** each input sits beside the results it affects. Once the setup is saved, each row shows what your change did.
- **Calculation Map:** a clickable map of how your inputs become results, with each formula filled in with your numbers. A **?** next to a number opens it.
- **Connect to Paddock:** one card shows whether you are connected and the one action you need, plus your last eight imports.

### The SlotForge look

Telemetry now shares its style with Timing and Paddock: the same title and number fonts, buttons, focus ring and tables, a slim top bar with status lights, and a Settings side list with quick unit toggles.

### Updates

Telemetry looks for a new version once at start. A window shows what is new and can download the file for your copy into your Downloads folder, with progress and a completeness check. Nothing is ever installed automatically, and **Settings → Updates** has *Check now* and a switch for the check.

### Safer data and fixes

- **Restores:** a restore interrupted by a crash or power cut is finished at the next start, so your data is never a mix of old and new. A full disk changes nothing. A backup with one unreadable file can still be restored.
- **Paddock imports:** a dropped connection during an import from Paddock on this computer now changes nothing, instead of saving with races missing.
- **Saves:** Telemetry tries again when Windows briefly holds a file, and clears leftovers of cut-off saves at start.
- **Library size and speed:** the Library now holds 500+ setups (it filled up at about 300), reads a large library about six times faster, and searches runs more quickly.
- **Smaller fixes:** source links under Driver Feedback advice open in your browser, a hidden invalid value no longer blocks Save without a message, values stay in your units, and about a dozen other page fixes.

### Review and compatibility

Local validation passed 292 automated tests and all 24 desktop suites. It also included new random-action and crash tests, network-cut tests, a 45-minute long run and a random-click run through the whole app.

Existing setups, lap data and backups remain readable. Favourites and run notes are stored so that older versions open the files and ignore them.

### Choose your download

The Windows files have new names, the same pattern as the other SlotForge apps.

| Computer | File in Assets |
| --- | --- |
| Windows, 64-bit Intel/AMD | **SlotForgeTelemetry-0.15.0-Setup-x64.exe**: installs with Start menu and desktop shortcuts. Or **…-Portable-x64.exe** to run without installing. |
| Apple Silicon or Intel Mac | **SlotForgeTelemetry-0.15.0-mac-universal.dmg**: open and drag into Applications. The ZIP contains the same app. |
| Ubuntu / Debian / Mint, x64 | **SlotForgeTelemetry-0.15.0-linux-amd64.deb**: open with your software installer. |
| Other Linux desktops, x64 | **SlotForgeTelemetry-0.15.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage**: allow execution in Properties, then open. |

GitHub's **Source code** archives are for developers. **SHA256SUMS.txt** contains checksums for the downloads.

### Updating

Close Telemetry and replace the old application with the new download, or run the installer. Your data is kept, and Telemetry makes a backup automatically.

See the [installation instructions](https://github.com/theDutchmanJames/SlotForgeTelemetry#how-to-install) for platform-specific help. Windows and macOS builds are not publisher-signed or notarized; the README explains the operating-system prompts.

Livery.body:
**SlotForge Livery 1.5.0 — The new look**

**A calmer look, rebuilt screens and stock cars to paint straight away**

## What's new

- **New look:** Graphite colours, new type and calmer buttons throughout Livery, with Light/Dark in the top right.
- **Paint Studio and Garage:** a Workbench layout, and one Garage page for cars, liveries, the library, the Trash and backups.
- **Showroom:** nine stock cars to paint when you don't have a drawing of your own.
- **Entries:** one livery on many cars, each with its own number and name.
- **Colours and printing:** livery colours with real paints and a shopping list, and a Print pack saved as one PDF.
- **Safer and faster:** exports and backups survive a crash, and the inspector and Print pack are much quicker.

## Everything in this release

**Look**
- A full restyle: Graphite colours, Barlow and Roboto Mono, flat buttons, quieter selections, and redesigned dialogs, Settings, Help and the welcome screen.
- The Light/Dark switch is back in the top right corner.

**Screens rebuilt**
- **Paint Studio:** Workbench layout with Layers on the left, view tabs, Selection and Workshop tabs, a quick bar and a right-click menu.
- **Garage:** one page for cars, liveries, the library, the Trash and backups.
- **Car setup:** a guided, step-by-step preparation of a new car.
- **Colours:** livery colours with real paints, the paints you own and a shopping list.
- **Print pack:** pick and order the pages, then save them as one PDF.
- **Side by side:** edit two sides together, mirrored or the same.
- **Help on the spot:** help for the screen you are on (F1), tours and a keyboard sheet.
- **Start page:** a proper welcome when you open Livery.
- **Arrivals:** imported packages arrive in the Garage, where you can check them or send them back.
- **Rescue window:** if the library cannot be read, Livery finds your backups and brings one back.

**New**
- **Entries:** one livery, many cars, each with its own number and name.
- **Showroom:** nine stock cars ready to paint.
- **Update window:** replaces the daily update check, shows what's new and downloads the update for you.

**Speed**
- The inspector is about five times faster; the Print pack draws about eight times faster.
- Side by side, Panel Studio and exports are quicker.

**Fixes**
- Exports and backups no longer damage an earlier file if Livery stops while writing; an interrupted restore leaves nothing behind.
- Typing a name and then clicking other artwork no longer renames the wrong piece.
- Liveries saved by older versions get their Garage summary rebuilt, so the Garage can group them.
- Two library items with the same id can no longer be merged silently.
- Opening a file that is not a Livery package gives a plain message.
- Many smaller fixes from a full review.

## Downloads

Every system has both an **installer** and a **portable app**:

- **Windows:** `…-windows-x64-setup.exe` (installer) or `…-windows-x64-portable.exe`.
- **macOS**, when supplied: `.dmg` (installer) or `.zip` (portable), for Intel (`x64`) and Apple silicon (`arm64`).
- **Linux:** `.deb` (installer) or `.AppImage` (portable), for x64 and arm64.

Both open the same library on a computer, so you can switch between them. EPS/PDF conversion is bundled and works offline. No account is required. Windows applications are unsigned; macOS packages are not notarised.

## Updating

Your existing library stays in the same location and opens as before. Designs that use the new features, such as Entries, may not show fully in older versions.

## Verification and source

Release assets are published only after their native build and packaged checks pass. This release also adds random-save, crash, random-click and coverage tests.

Livery is licensed under **GNU AGPL version 3 or later**. Corresponding source archives, build instructions and checksums accompany the downloads.

Decals.body:
**Platform availability:** Windows x64, macOS Intel, Linux x64 and Linux ARM64 are included. Native Apple Silicon downloads are built separately and added after testing.

# SlotForge Decals 0.4.0

Every screen redone, a new look shared with SlotForge Timing and Paddock, four more cars, and many fixes for safer saving and faster arranging.

## What's new

- **Workshop:** Decals now opens on a start page with all your sheets, their history and deleted sheets to recover.
- **Editor remade:** a slim top bar, a tool rail, Library/Layers/Pages tabs, Find (Ctrl+K) and a floating car fit check.
- **New pages:** a Decal Library with shelves and tags, a Car page to place the livery, and Print & share step by step.
- **Make on the sheet:** type text, racing numbers and shapes straight on the sheet; one Import bay for all artwork.
- **Four more cars:** classic and modern formula cars, a modern endurance prototype and a stock car.
- **Safer and faster:** autosave during non-stop editing, Undo on notices, and auto-arrange about 100× faster.

## A new look

- Calmer and clearer, shared with SlotForge Timing and Paddock: flat buttons, one red accent, **Barlow Condensed** titles and **Roboto Mono** numbers. Both fonts only style the app; your sheets and their fonts are untouched.
- The saved state is coloured: green when saved, yellow while saving, red if saving failed.

## Every screen redone

- **Workshop:** continue the open sheet, or start new: blank, from an image, from a shared file or the example. Every saved sheet with search, pin and filters, and a panel to open, rename, duplicate, share, pin, delete and see its history. Deleted sheets and snapshots can be recovered.
- **Editor:** a slim top bar with Find (Ctrl+K) and Export PDF; a tool rail with one-key shortcuts; Library, Layers and Pages tabs on the left; Decal, Layout and Sheet & paper tabs on the right. A selection bar above the selected decals, layers with thumbnails and locks, page thumbnails, and a zoom percentage with an actual-size button.
- **Import bay:** one window for all artwork, in steps: choose pages (PDF/EPS pages as separate decals), clean up, image or vector (trace), and size & place (on the car, quick sizes, 1, 2 or 4 copies).
- **Making artwork:** Text, Number and Shape: click to drop, drag to size, or Enter for free space. Type directly on the sheet with a small text bar. Racing numbers in rows, Recolour inside the Decal tab, and Edit vector over the sheet.
- **Decal Library page:** shelves for all, favourites, recently used, tags, untagged and each kind. Cards at the sheet's scale or true size. A details panel with tags, creator, sizes at 1:24, 1:32 and 1:43, and which sheets use the decal. Select several, and drag cards onto a tag shelf to tag them.
- **Layout tab:** align and space with exact spacing (with a note against the cutting gap), repeat with ghosts on the sheet, Most that fit, Fill the free space, page counts, and auto-arrange with a before/after preview.
- **Car page:** the whole livery on the side and top views, each decal at its printed size; drag to place and resize. Nine car bodies, or your own model from a photo.
- **Print & share page:** check the sheet (with one-click fixes), test print and measure, print on decal paper with white ink and cut lines, cut out for Silhouette, Cricut or ScanNCut, and share & back up.
- **Settings page:** the look, what Decals opens on, backups with a reminder, storage and updates. **Help** with three-step how-tos, Show me, and search. A **Fonts** tab with sample text, embedded fonts with clean-up, included fonts and computer fonts.
- **Clearer windows:** "Delete this?" windows say what will happen and what stays safe. Trouble cards start with "Your work is safe". Up to three notices at once, with Undo; a deleted sheet offers Recover.

## Update window

- About 5 seconds after Decals starts, it asks GitHub once whether a newer version is out. If there is one, a window shows the version, what is new in it, and the file for your copy (installer, portable app, disk image, AppImage or .deb).
- **Download** saves that file in your Downloads folder and checks it against the release; **Show in folder** then shows where it is. Decals never opens or installs it: close Decals and install it yourself.
- **Skip this version** hides the window until a newer version appears. **Settings → Updates** has Check now, and an on/off switch for the check at start.
- The Windows downloads are now named `Setup-x64.exe` and `Portable-x64.exe`, as in the other SlotForge apps.

## Fixes and speed

- **Safer saving:** auto-arrange and Undo no longer work from an out-of-date sheet; non-stop editing is now saved at most 2.5 seconds after the first change; closing right after an edit still saves it; interrupted backups and restores clean up their leftover files.
- **Print:** white ink works on long custom sheets, see-through decals keep their white, imported SVGs keep blend modes and hidden layers, and each font is in the print file once.
- **Clearer errors:** a damaged font says which font it is.
- **Faster:** auto-arrange with 300 decals went from 3.5 s to 0.03 s, filling a page is about 5× faster, and heavy image work runs in the background without freezing the editor. Snapshots are kept at least 10 minutes apart.

## Updating and installing

Your saved sheets and decals remain in **Documents/SlotForge Decals**, outside the application. Sheets from 0.4.0 open in 0.3.0 and the other way round. Back up first through **Settings → Backups → Back up now**.

| Computer | Installer | Portable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows x64 | Setup-x64.exe | Portable-x64.exe |
| Intel Mac | mac-x64.dmg | mac-x64.zip |
| Linux x64 | linux-amd64.deb | linux-x86_64.AppImage |
| Linux ARM64 | linux-arm64.deb | linux-arm64.AppImage |

The Windows installer installs for your user account only, lets you choose the folder and never deletes your workspace when uninstalling. Apple Silicon downloads are added after their separate build passes. Mac builds require macOS 15 or newer. Windows builds are unsigned; Smart App Control may block them. Mac builds are ad-hoc signed, not Apple-notarized. Updates are never installed automatically.

## Verification and sources

Local verification passed **171 unit tests** and **41 desktop suites** in both themes, all with workspaces isolated from user data. On top of those: a coverage map (90.6% of code lines run by the tests), thousands of seeded random save and undo sequences, tests that kill the app mid-save, and an hour of random clicking (45,846 steps, storage intact).

Licensed under **AGPL-3.0-or-later**; application source, corresponding Ghostscript and MuPDF sources, revision records and build instructions accompany the release. Bundled components retain their notices in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt.

Foundry.body:
A roof billboard prints face up, so its text can be raised like any sign.

## What's new

- **Roof billboards:** the two fins behind a roof billboard are parts of their own, so the board prints face up and its text is raised or cut in, as you choose.

## Details

**Roof billboards.** Until now the fins were part of the billboard, so it could only print face down and its text was always carved in V-grooves. Now the board prints flat on its back with its face up, and **Sign text** is raised 0.6 mm or, with **Cut in, not raised**, 0.6 mm deep, like a sign along the wall. Each fin prints lying on its side; glue it flat against the back of the board, 3 mm in from its end, its long side on the roof behind. The kit's README says where they go. A billboard saved before keeps its settings and is built the new way when opened. The Container café, the Refreshment kiosk, the Twin kiosk, the Ticket office and the Timing box have new pictures in **Start from**.

The [user guide](https://github.com/theDutchmanJames/SlotForgeFoundry/blob/v1.7.1/docs/GUIDE.md) explains every setting.

## Not yet printed

The new buildings, lettering, glazing templates and clearances of 1.7.0, and these fins, have been checked in software only: every part one piece, on the plate, without supports and clear of the others. The [notes of v1.7.0](https://github.com/theDutchmanJames/SlotForgeFoundry/releases/tag/v1.7.0) list what to try first.

## Verification

1149 unit tests passed on Windows, among them a billboard and its fins built on a flat, a sloped and a two-sided roof, each part whole, on the plate and printing without supports. The ten browser tests of the Buildings page and Home and the 69 checks of the main browser suite passed in the shipped app with networking disabled. The Windows desktop app started twice from its build and kept its Library and settings in the portable data folder.

The macOS and Linux downloads are built and tested by GitHub Actions after this release is published, on each operating system.

## Install

| System | Installer | Portable app |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | `SlotForgeFoundry-1.7.1-Setup-x64.exe` | `SlotForgeFoundry-1.7.1-Portable-x64.exe` |
| macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) | `SlotForgeFoundry-1.7.1-mac-universal.dmg` | `SlotForgeFoundry-1.7.1-mac-universal.zip` |
| Linux (x64) | `SlotForgeFoundry-1.7.1-linux-amd64.deb` | `SlotForgeFoundry-1.7.1-linux-x86_64.AppImage` |
| Linux (ARM) | `SlotForgeFoundry-1.7.1-linux-arm64.deb` | `SlotForgeFoundry-1.7.1-linux-arm64.AppImage` |
| Any browser | `SlotForge-Foundry-1.7.1.zip`: extract it and open **SlotForge Foundry.html** | |

Foundry is not code-signed. On Windows, choose **More info → Run anyway**. On macOS, use **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** the first time. On Linux, mark the AppImage as executable (`chmod +x`). The SHA256SUMS files list each download's checksum.

Your Library, layouts, buildings and settings carry over from earlier versions.

Anvil.body:
Clean up a laser-scanned body: grain off the panels, ragged rims straight.

## What's new

- **Smooth scan** (Repair › Smooth scan). For a body that was laser-scanned. It takes the grain out of the surface and straightens ragged rims around openings and cut edges, while creases and panel lines stay sharp and the body does not shrink.
  - You choose how far the surface may move at most, and how far the rims may move: no point goes further. A ragged rim waves further than the grain on a panel, so it has its own distance, and the surface beside a rim follows it, fading out.
  - Every move is checked, so no triangle turns over, and the mesh keeps every triangle: a closed body stays closed.
  - Raise **Strength** and the rim distance for a coarser scan. A new Smooth scan step goes before Hollow and the fitted details, so walls and windows are made on the cleaned body. Compare with **Original** under Look.

## Project files

A project that uses Smooth scan is saved in a newer project format, so Anvil 1.1.5 and older refuse to open it with a message instead. Every other project opens in older versions as before. To share such a body with someone on an older Anvil, send the exported STL.

## Verification

196 unit tests passed on Windows, none skipped, including 5 new ones: grain on a test cube goes while its edges stay sharp and its size stays the same; ragged cube edges are straightened within the rim distance; and a test car is smoothed with no triangle turned over, nothing moved further than allowed and the mesh still closed. In the app, a laser-scanned body of a million triangles was cleaned up in about 10 seconds with no open or faulty edges; applying, updating, undo, redo, editing the step and its place before Hollow were checked. The desktop app was started twice on a fresh data folder. The macOS and Linux downloads are built and tested by GitHub Actions after this release is published, on each operating system.

## Install

| System | Installer | Portable app |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | `SlotForgeAnvil-1.1.6-Setup-x64.exe` | `SlotForgeAnvil-1.1.6-Portable-x64.exe` or `SlotForgeAnvil-1.1.6-Windows-x64.zip` |
| macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) | `SlotForgeAnvil-1.1.6-mac-universal.dmg` | `SlotForgeAnvil-1.1.6-mac-universal.zip` |
| Linux (x64) | `SlotForgeAnvil-1.1.6-linux-amd64.deb` | `SlotForgeAnvil-1.1.6-linux-x86_64.AppImage` |
| Linux (ARM) | `SlotForgeAnvil-1.1.6-linux-arm64.deb` | `SlotForgeAnvil-1.1.6-linux-arm64.AppImage` |

Anvil is not code-signed. On Windows, choose **More info → Run anyway**. On macOS, use **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** the first time. On Linux, mark the AppImage as executable (`chmod +x`). The SHA256SUMS files list each download's checksum.

Your projects, library and settings carry over. Anvil 1.0.1 and later tell you about this version themselves.

Frame.body:
SlotForge Frame 0.7.1 lets you measure positions from the rear axle.

## New

- **Measure from the front or the rear axle:** a **From** switch at the bottom of the window, next to mm / in, sets where positions along the car count from. With **Rear axle** chosen:
  - every along position counts forward from the rear axle, and behind it is negative. This covers the panels, the outline and other point lists, the cross rails, the body mounts, the split cut and the fold lines. The front axle then reads +wheelbase.
  - Peter's 1:43 Chassis settings measured from the plate's front switch to the rear axle too.
  - the centre of gravity readout and the clash message count from the rear axle.
  - a red 0 marks the rear axle in the top view.
  - new shaping features keep their place from the rear axle when the wheelbase changes.
  - in Arrange features and Position reference, positive means forward.
- **Saved designs are unchanged:** the choice is saved with each design, and positions are still stored from the front axle. Older projects open as before.

## Verification

- 195 unit tests and 39 browser checks pass, including a check that a value typed from the rear axle is stored correctly.
- The desktop start-up test passes on the packaged Windows app. GitHub Actions builds the macOS and Linux downloads and runs the start-up test on each system before attaching them.

| System | Installer | Portable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `SlotForgeFrame-0.7.1-Setup-x64.exe` | `SlotForgeFrame-0.7.1-Portable-x64.exe` or `SlotForgeFrame-0.7.1-Windows-x64.zip` |
| macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) | `SlotForgeFrame-0.7.1-mac-universal.dmg` | `SlotForgeFrame-0.7.1-mac-universal.zip` |
| Linux x64 | `SlotForgeFrame-0.7.1-linux-amd64.deb` | `SlotForgeFrame-0.7.1-linux-x86_64.AppImage` |
| Linux arm64 | `SlotForgeFrame-0.7.1-linux-arm64.deb` | `SlotForgeFrame-0.7.1-linux-arm64.AppImage` |

The macOS and Linux files are added to this release a few minutes after it is published. Each system has a `SHA256SUMS` file to check a download against.

The downloads are not code signed. Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper may ask you to confirm before the app opens for the first time.
